feedback: The candidate is valid. Its five 8 mm sensors at x = -0.016 to +0.016 and y = 0.03 match iteration 1, the best raced design (65.9, 8 mm sensors, kp 2.0, kd 0.2, base 1.5). Its weights are antisymmetric in [-2, 2], and kp, ki, kd, base_speed and line_loss are in range. Nothing is obviously broken. The change is ki 0.05 to 0.8 with base_speed 1.5 to 1.3. Iterations 0 to 2 all ended off_track on every trial, with max_error about 0.061 to 0.064 and one or two line-loss events per run. That constant max_error fits a robot that reaches the tape edge on bends. It is not clear evidence of a steady bias, so the rationale's motor-mismatch diagnosis is a hypothesis, not a finding. Raising ki 16-fold is a large step. The integral is capped at +/-2, so the integral term can add up to 1.6 to the turn, which is enough to change steering. Lowering base_speed to 1.3 also confounds the test, and it works against the 1.5 m/s average the course needs. Progress on a run that stays on track may therefore fall, even if line loss improves. This is early exploration with 8 iterations left, and no build has finished, so telemetry from this race is worth more than another revision made without it. The next critique should use the race result. If line_loss_events drop and progress rises, keep ki and move base_speed back toward 1.5. If the run oscillates or max_error grows, reduce ki to about 0.3 before changing kp. If max_error stays near 0.061 with ki high, the drift is not a steady bias, so return to iteration 1 and test kp or sensor placement instead.
requested_changes: If the race shows steady drift in one direction (large rms_error with a stable sign) and line_loss_events fall, keep ki near 0.8 and raise base_speed from 1.3 back toward 1.5 in steps, since the 1.3 setting may not cover the course in time.
If steering_oscillation rises or max_error grows with ki at 0.8, reduce ki to about 0.3 before changing kp, because the integral term is the most likely new source of jitter.

If max_error stays near 0.061 with ki high and no drift signature, revert ki to 0.05 and test kp 2.5 with the iteration 1 geometry, since the constant max_error points to edge-of-line loss on bends rather than a bias.
